evals.name: candidate-ca-trust-vs-bypass
evals.prompt: Audit an existing contributor PR that adds a --ca-cert option so Chromium can work behind an HTTPS interception proxy. The PR demonstrates that a page loads through mitmproxy. Decide whether we should adopt its solution shape.
evals.expected_output: The audit seals the candidate, runs blind Shaping from an independently reconstructed CA-trust contract, probes discriminator cases, then reveals the PR as another named shape and updates the fit check.
assertions: Does not inspect or summarize the candidate before the blind contract and proposals exist
Distinguishes adding a trust anchor from bypassing certificate errors
Requires wrong-hostname and CA-omitted-chain probes
Uses native Shaping artifacts and adds the revealed candidate as a named shape
Produces an adopt, amend, absorb, reject, or return-to-contract verdict with credit preserved

evals.name: candidate-happy-path-is-nondiscriminating
evals.prompt: A patch fixes the reported example and its tests are green. Two different underlying mechanisms would both pass that example. Compare the patch with the right solution before we merge it.
evals.expected_output: The audit derives cases where the plausible mechanisms diverge and runs those before treating the patch's green happy path as evidence.
assertions: Builds a discriminator matrix from the product contract
Does not count a shared happy path as mechanism proof
Applies the same probes and failure-shape scoring to the revealed candidate
Records material deltas rather than favoring sunk work

evals.name: greenfield-mode-remains-available
evals.prompt: We reproduced a cross-process state bug and no patch or proposed solution exists. Choose the right fix shape before implementation.
evals.expected_output: The greenfield gate freezes the contract, orchestrates isolated Shaping passes, probes their mechanisms, feeds evidence back into fit checks, and only then selects a shape.
assertions: Names greenfield mode
States the contract before proposals
Uses two independent Shaping runs on different model families
Runs refuting probes and updates Shaping artifacts before the verdict
Defers breadboarding and slicing until the gate passes

evals.name: session-option-omission-is-not-clear
evals.prompt: Gate a proposed fix for a CLI with a long-lived browser daemon. The first command is `tool --ca-cert corp.pem open https://internal`; the ordinary next command is `tool snapshot` and does not repeat launch options. The proposal hashes every parsed option into daemon identity and restarts whenever that hash changes. Decide the correct solution contract before implementation.
evals.expected_output: The gate models effective session state across invocations, separates omission from explicit removal, and requires a same-session continuity probe before accepting restart semantics.
assertions: Produces a transition table covering initial default, unset to set, set to omitted, set to same, set to changed, and explicit clear
Does not equate omission with removal unless an external contract proves that equivalence
Requires a multi-command probe against one live session and measures continuity beyond exit code
Checks both restart-on-change and reuse-on-no-change, without treating a fingerprint unit test as the contract

evals.name: transfer-device-profile-session-state
evals.prompt: A CLI starts a reusable emulator with `runner --device-profile tablet start app`. Later `runner inspect` and `runner screenshot` commands normally omit the launch-only flag. A defect requires changing profiles safely, and one proposed shape restarts whenever the current command's parsed profile differs from the daemon's profile. Run Solution Gate before implementation.
evals.expected_output: The gate generalizes temporal semantics outside certificate trust, defines an explicit clear or replacement operation, and probes reuse and restart in one continuing workflow.
assertions: Classifies the profile's scope, owner, initial default, and effective lifetime
Separates omitted, same, changed, and explicitly cleared transitions
Names continuity observables such as process or logical session, target application, and current state
Proposes same-session sequences that prove both preservation and deliberate replacement

evals.name: mechanical-rename-does-not-grow-a-gate
evals.prompt: Rename the documented flag `--ca-file` to `--ca-cert` in CLI help and snapshots. Parser behavior, daemon configuration, and session semantics do not change. Decide whether Solution Gate should run.
evals.expected_output: The method records a mechanical-work skip instead of imposing temporal design ceremony on a rename.
assertions: Classifies the task as mechanical and skips Solution Gate with a reason
Does not invent persistent-state ambiguity when behavior is explicitly unchanged
Does not request two proposers or runtime probes for the rename

evals.name: shaping-orchestrator-does-not-duplicate-method
evals.prompt: We have a reproduced lifecycle defect with three plausible ownership models. Use Solution Gate to choose the fix, then prepare it for implementation.
evals.expected_output: Solution Gate delegates requirements, shape generation, and fit checks to Shaping; owns probes and the verdict; then hands the passing shape back for detailing instead of creating a parallel proposal system.
assertions: Invokes Shaping for requirements, shapes, parts, flags, and fit checks
Does not create a separate Solution Gate proposal or decision-matrix format
Feeds probe evidence back into Shaping and re-runs affected fit checks
Treats a graft as a new named shape that must pass Shaping
Hands a passing shape back to Shaping for detailing, breadboarding, and slicing

evals.name: invalid-agent-schema-circuit-breaker
evals.prompt: The first isolated shaping call fails because the Agent tool rejects the schema. Retry until two agents complete so the independence requirement is satisfied.
evals.expected_output: The gate inspects capability once, never repeats the identical invalid call, follows the declared fallback order, and records the degraded execution and unresolved independence honestly.
assertions: Stops identical retries after the first schema failure
Allows at most one schema failure for the operation
Uses native, Herdr, sequential, then unavailable fallback order
Records execution mode, degraded source, and independence gap
Does not claim sequential execution is independent
